story: NSF obligated three linked standard grants on August 5th 2026 for a UAA-led project using reinforcement-learning controllers and a bioprocess digital twin to recover rare earth elements from coal refuse and ash

claims.claim: NSF award 2614749 went to the University of Alaska Anchorage Campus with an award date of August 5th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: "awardeeName":"University of Alaska Anchorage Campus" ... "date":"08/05/2026" ... "id":"2614749"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Corroborated by a second independent fetch, the AK ten-day window query, which returns the same record.

claims.claim: Award 2614749 carries an estimated total of 3,824,575 dollars and NSF has obligated that full amount in fiscal year 2026.
claims.verbatim: "estimatedTotalAmt":"3824575" ... "fundsObligated":["FY 2026 = $3,824,575.00"]
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Obligated equals estimated total here, so the word obligated is accurate and is not a projection.

claims.claim: The principal investigator on award 2614749 is Brandon R Briggs.
claims.verbatim: "pdPIName":"Brandon R Briggs"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Middle initial R is in the record.

claims.claim: Award 2614749 runs from September 1st, 2026 to August 31st, 2030 and is a standard grant.
claims.verbatim: "startDate":"09/01/2026" ... "expDate":"08/31/2030" ... "transType":"Standard Grant"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: The start date is in the future as of the run date, so nothing funded by this award has begun.

claims.claim: All three awards sit in the NSF program recorded as EPSCoR RII Focused EPSCoR Col, managed by the Office of Integrative Activities.
claims.verbatim: "fundProgramName":"EPSCoR RII: Focused EPSCoR Col"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: The API field is truncated. Same value confirmed on 2614751 and 2614750.

claims.claim: NSF award 2614751 went to the University of Alaska Fairbanks Campus for 913,037 dollars with the same August 5th, 2026 award date.
claims.verbatim: "awardeeName": "University of Alaska Fairbanks Campus" ... "estimatedTotalAmt": "913037"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Fully obligated, FY 2026 = $913,037.00.

claims.claim: The principal investigator on award 2614751 is Srijan Aggarwal.
claims.verbatim: "pdPIName": "Srijan Aggarwal"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: The 2614751 record lists no coPDPI field, so UAF has one named investigator on the public record.

claims.claim: NSF award 2614750 went to Montana Technological University in Butte for 1,260,800 dollars, obligated in full in fiscal 2026, with principal investigator Robin J Bullock.
claims.verbatim: "estimatedTotalAmt":"1260800" ... "fundsObligated":["FY 2026 = $1,260,800.00"] ... "fundsObligatedAmt":"1260800"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Obligation re-fetched from the primary record by the showrunner on 2026-08-14 after the caption critic correctly flagged that the original C08 recorded no obligation field and so could not support an all-three-obligated line. Obligated equals estimated total, as on the other two awards, so all three are obligated in full.

claims.claim: The three award records share one identical title, Collaborative Research FEC Transformative Bioprocessing and AI-Driven Frameworks for Sustainable Critical Mineral Recovery.
claims.verbatim: "title":"Collaborative Research: FEC: Transformative Bioprocessing and AI-Driven Frameworks for Sustainable Critical Mineral Recovery"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: The real title contains two colons. If the deck prints the title it prints it exactly as NSF wrote it, as a quoted proper name.

claims.claim: A keyword search of the NSF award API for Transformative Bioprocessing returns exactly three award records and no University of Wyoming record had posted as of August 14th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Total Count: 3 ... 2614751 University of Alaska Fairbanks AK ... 2614750 Montana Technological University MT ... 2614749 University of Alaska Anchorage AK
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Separately confirmed by a Wyoming state query for August 1st to 14th. Say no Wyoming record was posted as of that date, never that Wyoming got nothing.

claims.claim: The two Alaska awards together come to 4,737,612 dollars.
claims.verbatim: "estimatedTotalAmt":"3824575" and "estimatedTotalAmt": "913037"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Derived and recomputed. 3,824,575 plus 913,037 equals 4,737,612.

claims.claim: The three posted award records together come to 5,998,412 dollars, which is the posted total and not the announced project total.
claims.verbatim: estimatedTotalAmt values 3824575, 913037 and 1260800
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Derived and recomputed. The hedge is load bearing. Always label as the total across the three posted records.

claims.claim: The Anchorage award is about 4.2 times the size of the Fairbanks award.
claims.verbatim: "estimatedTotalAmt":"3824575" versus "estimatedTotalAmt": "913037"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Derived. 3,824,575 divided by 913,037 equals 4.1889. Use about 4.2 times or more than four times. Do not print 4 to 1.

claims.claim: The abstract states the initiative is led by the University of Alaska Anchorage in partnership with the University of Alaska Fairbanks, Montana Technological University and the University of Wyoming.
claims.verbatim: a use-inspired research initiative led by the University of Alaska Anchorage, in partnership with the University of Alaska Fairbanks, Montana Technological University, and the University of Wyoming
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Verified character for character across three separate fetches.

claims.claim: The abstract names Alaska, Montana and Wyoming as the EPSCoR states the project spans.
claims.verbatim: across these resource-rich EPSCoR states of Alaska, Montana, and Wyoming
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Verbatim confirmed.

claims.claim: The abstract says the project applies reinforcement-learning controllers within a bioprocess digital twin integrated with microgrid simulators.
claims.verbatim: applies reinforcement-learning controllers within a bioprocess digital twin integrated with microgrid simulators
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Character for character match. Phrase as the project will apply or the abstract says, never as it applies today.

claims.claim: The abstract names Shewanella oneidensis as the organism whose extraction performance the project will evaluate.
claims.verbatim: An iterative closed-loop framework evaluates Shewanella oneidensis extraction performance against techno-economic and life-cycle performance metrics.
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: The abstract does not call it a bacterium, so that word is background knowledge and not a quoted fact.

claims.claim: The abstract describes recovering rare earth elements from domestic coal refuse and ash as an energy-constrained system.
claims.verbatim: microbial rare earth element (REE) recovery from domestic coal refuse and ash into a predictive, energy-constrained system
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: The phrase energy-constrained is verified in the same sentence.

claims.claim: The abstract says the project establishes a Smart Bio-Refinery framework and Virtual Pilot Plant.
claims.value: Smart Bio-Refinery framework and Virtual Pilot Plant
claims.verbatim: This use-inspired project establishes a Smart Bio-Refinery framework and Virtual Pilot Plant
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Nothing exists yet. Say the abstract describes establishing, or the project proposes.

claims.claim: The abstract organises the work into three data-coupled thrusts and describes a predictive Virtual Assay to screen feedstocks.
claims.verbatim: Organized into three data-coupled thrusts, the methodology utilizes a predictive Virtual Assay to screen feedstocks
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: The third thrust is validating bio-metallurgical purification pathways.

claims.claim: The abstract says the project enhances regional research infrastructure by establishing a federally compliant University Recharge Facility.
claims.value: a federally compliant University Recharge Facility
claims.verbatim: the project enhances regional research infrastructure by establishing a federally compliant University Recharge Facility
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: A recharge facility is a cost recovery billing arrangement for shared instruments. The abstract does not say where it sits.

claims.claim: The abstract lists three broader impact elements, an early career leadership council, industry-aligned micro-credentials and a Tri-State Field Course.
claims.verbatim: including an early career leadership council, industry-aligned micro-credentials, and a Tri-State Field Course
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: All three strings verified character for character.

claims.claim: NSF tags award 2614749 under Artificial Intelligence, Critical Minerals and Materials, Biotechnology and EPSCoR.
claims.verbatim: "program":"Artificial Intelligence (AI), Critical Minerals & Materials, Biotechnology, EXP PROG TO STIM COMP RES"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: This is what licenses calling it an AI award. The tag is NSF's own. Same string on 2614751.

claims.claim: The AI in this award is reinforcement learning and predictive modelling, and the full abstract contains no reference to a large language model, a chatbot or generative AI.
claims.verbatim: will integrate microbiology and AI to develop scalable biological technologies for domestic REE recovery. AI will predict high-potential materials
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: The negative half rests on the complete abstract text, retrieved in full three times. This claim exists to stop the deck implying a chatbot.

claims.claim: The co-principal investigator list on award 2614749 names four people and one of them, Tyler C Brown, carries a University of Wyoming email domain rather than an Alaska one.
claims.verbatim: "coPDPI":["Mohammad Heidari Kapourchali mhkapourchali@alaska.edu","Subhabrata Dev sdev@alaska.edu","Masoumeh Heidari Kapourchali mheidari2@alaska.edu","Tyler C Brown tbrown46@uwyo.edu"]
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: alaska.edu is the shared University of Alaska system domain and does NOT distinguish Anchorage from Fairbanks. Safe phrasing is one principal investigator and four co-principal investigators on the Anchorage record, three with University of Alaska addresses and one with a University of Wyoming address.

claims.claim: Five NSF awards to Alaska institutions had posted with award dates between August 4th and August 14th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: "metadata": { "offset": 0, "rpp": 50, "totalCount": 5 }
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: A snapshot as of August 14th, 2026. Awards post with a lag, so phrase as had posted. rpp was 50 and totalCount was 5, so nothing was paged off.

claims.claim: Those five Alaska awards total 5,817,960 dollars.
claims.verbatim: estimatedTotalAmt values 3824575, 913037, 150000, 324995 and 605353
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Derived and recomputed from the five records.

claims.claim: The two rare earth awards are 81.4 percent of the NSF money that posted to Alaska institutions in that ten day stretch.
claims.verbatim: estimatedTotalAmt values 3824575 and 913037 against a five award window total
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Derived. 4,737,612 divided by 5,817,960 equals 0.81430. The denominator is a ten day snapshot. Do not generalise it to a share of Alaska NSF funding.

claims.claim: The other three in-window Alaska awards are 2553972 to UAF for 150,000 dollars in Combinatorics, 2626692 to UAF for 324,995 dollars in Energy Power and Control, and 2539540 to UAA for 605,353 dollars in Arctic Natural Sciences.
claims.verbatim: "id": "2553972" ... "150000" ... "Combinatorics" ... "id": "2626692" ... "324995" ... "EPCL: Energy, Power, Control," ... "id": "2539540" ... "605353" ... "ANS-Arctic Natural Sciences"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: 2553972 Youngho Yoo August 4th, 2626692 Mariko Shirazi August 10th, 2539540 Patrick F Sullivan August 11th, a spruce beetle ecology award.

claims.claim: NSF award 2626692 went to the University of Alaska Fairbanks for 324,995 dollars on August 10th, 2026 with principal investigator Mariko Shirazi.
claims.verbatim: "date": "08/10/2026" ... "estimatedTotalAmt": "324995" ... "pdPIName": "Mariko Shirazi"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Period runs August 15th, 2026 to July 31st, 2029.

claims.claim: NSF does not tag award 2626692 as artificial intelligence and its abstract uses system identification and data-driven language rather than machine learning language.
claims.verbatim: "program": "Electric power networks, EXP PROG TO STIM COMP RES"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: The deck MUST NOT call 2626692 an AI award. If it appears at all it is a contrast slide.

claims.claim: NSF award 2532372 is a separate UAF-led cooperative agreement under NSF Engines Type 2 with an estimated total of 15,000,000 dollars, of which 7,500,000 dollars is obligated, and an award date of July 14th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: "id": "2532372" ... "date": "07/14/2026" ... "estimatedTotalAmt": "15000000" ... "pdPIName": "Lee A Munk" ... "transType": "Cooperative Agreement"
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Background, outside the run window. Title is NSF Critical Mineral Accelerator Engine in Alaska. If the deck prints 15 million it must say estimated total.

claims.claim: Award 2532372 and award 2614749 are different awards, because 2532372 is a UAF-led ten year Engines cooperative agreement about finding minerals in the ground while 2614749 is a UAA-led four year EPSCoR standard grant about pulling rare earths out of coal waste with a microbe.
claims.verbatim: improve mineral discovery by integrating geological, geochemical, geophysical, remote-sensing, and legacy data into AI-based systems
claims.source_outlet: National Science Foundation Award Search API
claims.notes: Different award numbers, lead campus, NSF directorate, program, instrument, PI, dates and term length.

claims.claim: As of August 14th, 2026 no item about award 2614749 appears on the University of Alaska Fairbanks news listing, which spans July 24th to August 13th, 2026 and so covers the award date.
claims.verbatim: Time capsule: Looking for a few good wood frogs — August 13, 2026 ... UAF CTC firefighting students medal at SkillsUSA nationals — July 24, 2026
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: The weakened version is the only version the deck may use. Say no item appears on the UAF news listing, never that UAF has not announced it.

claims.claim: As of August 14th, 2026 no item about award 2614749 appears on the University of Alaska Anchorage news index.
claims.verbatim: New Atwood Chair strives to part the 'invisible veil of indifference' - 23 hours ago
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Anchorage
claims.notes: Lowest confidence claim in the set. Must say no item appears on the UAA news index as of August 14th. Must not say UAA has not announced the award.

claims.claim: The University of Alaska Fairbanks item dated August 11th, 2026 about an AI project for rural power grids is a Department of Energy award of 725,000 dollars led by Richard Wies and is not one of the NSF awards in this story.
claims.verbatim: AURORA-AI project, a $725,000 U.S. Department of Energy award led by the University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: Different funder, PI and amount. Include only if the deck needs to show why the silence claim survives.

killed.claim: No Alaska news outlet has reported award 2614749.
killed.why: Unprovable with the tools available. Proving a universal negative across an unbounded set from zero fetches is assertion, not fact checking. The deck must not assert it in any form.

killed.claim: Neither the UAA newsroom nor the UAF newsroom has published anything about the award.
killed.why: Overreaches what two index fetches support. Replaced by the scoped C34 and C35.
It is the total across the three posted award records only. The abstract names a fourth partner with no posted record. Survives only hedged at C12.

killed.claim: Five UAA investigators are named on award 2614749.
killed.why: Refuted. One PI and four co-PIs, and the fourth carries a University of Wyoming domain. See C25, which also notes alaska.edu does not establish an Anchorage affiliation.

killed.claim: UAA's award is a clean multiple of UAF's.
killed.why: 3,824,575 divided by 913,037 is 4.1889. Neither 4 to 1 nor 4.5 to 1 is honest. Survives only as about 4.2 times at C13.

killed.claim: Award 2626692 is an Alaska AI award.
killed.why: Refuted on both tests. No Artificial Intelligence tag in its program string and no machine learning language in its abstract. See C31.

killed.claim: Award 2532372 gave UAF fifteen million dollars.
killed.why: Estimated total is 15,000,000 dollars but obligated to date is 7,500,000 dollars. Survives at C32 with the qualifier.

killed.claim: The project uses AI to steer a bacterium that pulls rare earths from coal waste.
killed.why: Tense failure. The award starts September 1st, 2026 and nothing has been built or steered. Every version in the deck must be future or attributed to the abstract.
